It is a part of [[Om Prakash Jindal|OP Jindal group]]. The firm has a melt capacity of 2.9 million tonnes per annum which makes it the largest stainless steel producer of India. Incorporated in 1970, it ranks among the top 5 stainless steel makers of the world.{{cite web |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/industry/jindal-stainless-targets-top-3-spot-globally-lines-up-rs-2-5-crore-capex/3091853/ |title= Jindal Stainless targets top-3 spot globally; lines up Rs 2.5-crore capex |publisher=financialexpress.com |access-date=18 May 2023}}{{cite web |url=https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/jindal-stainless-announces-special-interim-dividend-for-fy-22-23-record-date-fixed-11681816448252.html |title=Jindal Stainless Announces Special Interim Dividend |publisher=livemint.com |access-date=11 May 2023}} Jindal Stainless has two stainless steel manufacturing complexes in India, in the states of [[Haryana]] and [[Odisha]] and one overseas manufacturing unit in Indonesia. It has 14 global offices across the world.{{cite web |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/company-facts/jindalstainless/history/JSL01 |title= Company History:Jindal Stainless |publisher=moneycontrol.com |access-date=11 May 2023}} Its Managing Director, [[Abhyuday Jindal]] is the current president of the [[Indian Chamber of Commerce]].{{Cite web |last=shivampatel1 |date=2024-10-21 |title=Abhyuday Jindal Named New President of Indian Chamber of Commerce |url=https://currentaffairs.adda247.com/abhyuday-jindal-named-new-president-of-indian-chamber-of-commerce/ |access-date=2024-10-21 |website=adda247 |language=en-IN}} ==History== In 1970, O.P. Jindal founded a mini steel plant named Jindal Strips Limited at [[Hisar (city)|Hisar]].{{cite web |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/jindal-stainless-ltd-expects-20-volume-growth-following-removal-of-export-restrictions-and-surge-in-domestic-demand-11684342913907.html |title= JSL Expects volume to grow by 20% this fiscal |publisher=livemint.com |access-date=18 May 2023}} It started manufacturing hot rolled carbon steel coils, plates, slabs and blooms. It was the beginning of the story for Jindal Stainless. Over the years, the company expanded its capacity at Hisar. In 2002, Jindal Strips was restructured as Jindal Stainless. In 2003, Jindal Stainless set up its integrated stainless steel plant at Jajpur in Odisha with a capacity scalable up to 3.2 MTPA. The plant became operational in 2011.{{cite web |url=https://www.equitypandit.com/jindal-stainless-shares-rise-7-after-q4-profit-beats-forecasts/ |title= Jindal Stainless Shares Rise 7% After Q4 Profit Beats Forecasts|date= 18 May 2023|publisher=equitypandit.com |access-date=18 May 2023}} ==Production== The plants of Jindal Stainless are located in [[Jajpur]], Odisha and Hisar, Haryana.{{cite web |url=https://www.ndtv.com/business/stock/jindal-stainless-ltd_jsl/reports |title=Jindal Stainless Ltd |publisher=ndtv.com.com |access-date=11 May 2023}} The Jajpur facility started operating in 1970 while the Hisar plant was made operational in the year 1975. The plants comprise 2.9 million tonnes per annum of stainless steel melting facilities. The Jajpur plant has a melting capacity of 2.1 MTPA. The plant has a captive power generation facility of 264 MW. The Hisar plant has a melting capacity of 0.8 MTPA. It is also India's largest producer of coin blanks. Jindal Stainless steel unveiled world's first off-grid Green hydrogen based Stainless steel plant in Hisar, Haryana with technology from Hygenco, a [[Gurgaon]] based renewable firm.{{cite web | title=India - the world's second-largest producer of crude steel goes green with Green Hydrogen | date=16 March 2024 | url=https://www.hydrogennewsletter.com/india-the-worlds-second-largest-producer-of-crude-steel-go-green-with-green-hydrogen/ }}{{Cite web | title=Press Release:Press Information Bureau | url=https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2011214 | access-date=2025-12-30 | website=www.pib.gov.in}} ==Products== JSL produces a variety of products in both facilities.
